**Random walks remember shocks, so unrelated series can appear to move together for long periods.** Each new innovation changes the level permanently. Two independent walks may both wander upward over a sample, producing a visually persuasive regression even though neither drives the other. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/)

Conventional regression t-statistics assume error behavior that this level-on-level regression may violate. Many observations along one slow excursion do not provide the same independent evidence as many unrelated draws. High R-squared and a small conventional p-value can therefore be spurious.

**Cointegration asks a stronger, different question.** If two nonstationary series share a stable long-run relation, some combination such as $Y_t-\beta X_t$ can be stationary. For example, let X be a random walk and let $Y_t=2X_t+u_t$ with stationary u. Both levels wander, but Y-2X fluctuates around a stable distribution.

Engle–Granger evaluates a fitted residual relation using appropriate critical values; Johansen handles multivariate relations. Independent random walks do not become cointegrated merely because their sample correlation is high. For any strategy evaluation, estimate using past data, account for selection among many pairs, test breaks, and include execution costs. A statistical relation is not by itself evidence of a profitable executable trade.

**Technical details and references.**

Independent random walks can share long smooth excursions by chance. Regressing their levels violates usual stationary-error assumptions, so high $R^2$ and conventional t-statistics can be spurious. Differencing removes a unit root but may discard a meaningful long-run relation if one exists. [1](https://otexts.com/fpp3/)

Cointegration means a nontrivial linear combination of integrated series is stationary, for example $Y_t-\beta X_t$. Engle–Granger tests residual behavior with appropriate nonstandard critical values; Johansen handles multiple series/relations.

A cointegrating relation is not automatically a profitable pairs strategy. Test stability, estimate using past data only, model execution costs, and monitor breaks. Repeatedly searching many pairs creates selection bias; a favorable residual test on the chosen pair needs independent validation.
